senses.gloss:
भैक्ष भैक्ष, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भिक्षा), living
by alms, subsisting by charity; (अम्), n. asking alms,
begging, mendicancy, (भैक्षं चर् or भै-
क्षाय गम्, to go about begging, beg); anything
obtained by begging, begged food, charity, alms.
—भैक्ष-काल, अस्, m. ‘alms-time,’ the time for
alms or for bringing home anything obtained as
alms.
—भैक्ष-चरण or भैक्ष-चर्य, अम्,
n. or भैक्ष-चर्या, f. the going about begging,
plying for alms, collecting alms, begging.
—भै-
क्ष-जीविका, f. living on alms, subsisting by begging,
mendicancy.
—भैक्ष-भुज्, क्, क्, क्, eating alms-
food, living on alms; (क्), m. a mendicant.
—भै-
क्ष-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the living on alms, mendicancy;
(इस्, इस्, इ), living by charity.
—भैक्षान्न (˚ष-
अन्˚), अम्, n. ‘alms-food,’ food obtained as alms,
begged food.
—भैक्षाशिन् (˚ष-आश्˚), ई, इनी, इ,
eating alms-food or food obtained by begging; (ई),
m. a mendicant.
—भैक्षाश्य, अम्, n. (fr. the
preceding), the living on alms, subsisting by charity.
—भैक्षाहार (˚ष-आह्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, eating
begged food or food given in charity; (अस्), m. one
living on charity (Manu XI. 257), a mendicant.

भैक्षक (at the end of an adj. comp.) =
भैक्ष, alms.

भैक्षुक, अम्, n. (fr. भिक्षुक), a number of
mendicants, assemblage or collection of beggars.

भैक्ष्य, an incorrect form for भैक्ष above.
—भैक्ष्य-काल, भैक्ष्य-चर्य, भैक्ष्य-
वृत्ति, see भैक्ष-काल, &c.
